R Markdown (`.Rmd`) and Quarto (`.qmd`) use Pandoc to turn citation keys into
formatted citations and a reference list. The two formats use the same BibTeX
bibliography files, citation syntax, and Citation Style Language (CSL) files.

## Create a BibTeX bibliography

Store references in a plain-text file with a `.bib` extension. Each entry has a
type, a unique citation key, and fields describing the source. For example,
save the following as `references.bib` next to your manuscript:

```bibtex
@article{wickham2014,
  author  = {Wickham, Hadley},
  title   = {Tidy Data},
  journal = {Journal of Statistical Software},
  year    = {2014},
  volume  = {59},
  number  = {10},
  pages   = {1--23},
  doi     = {10.18637/jss.v059.i10}
}

@book{xie2018,
  author    = {Xie, Yihui and Allaire, J. J. and Grolemund, Garrett},
  title     = {R Markdown: The Definitive Guide},
  publisher = {Chapman and Hall/CRC},
  year      = {2018},
  url       = {https://bookdown.org/yihui/rmarkdown/}
}

@misc{quarto2026,
  author = {{Posit Software, PBC}},
  title  = {Quarto Documentation},
  year   = {2026},
  url    = {https://quarto.org/docs/}
}
```

The citation keys in this example are `wickham2014`, `xie2018`, and
`quarto2026`. Reference managers such as Zotero can export an entire library or
a selected collection as BibTeX.

## Connect the bibliography to a document

Add the bibliography path to the document's YAML header. The path is relative
to the `.Rmd` or `.qmd` file.

For an R Markdown manuscript:

````markdown
---
title: "My manuscript"
output: word_document
bibliography: references.bib
---
````

For a Quarto manuscript:

````markdown
---
title: "My manuscript"
format: docx
bibliography: references.bib
---
````

Both formats also accept multiple bibliography files:

```yaml
bibliography:
  - references.bib
  - software.bib
```

## Cite sources in the text

Use the entry's citation key after an `@`:

```markdown
Wickham (@wickham2014) describes a consistent structure for tidy data.

R Markdown supports reproducible manuscripts [@xie2018].

Several tools support this workflow [@xie2018; @quarto2026].

The relevant discussion appears in a specific section [@xie2018, sec. 2.8].
```

These forms produce narrative, parenthetical, multiple, and located citations,
respectively. The first two forms render in this vignette as follows:
Wickham (@wickham2014) describes a consistent structure for tidy data, and R
Markdown supports reproducible manuscripts [@xie2018].

Pandoc creates the reference list from cited entries. To include every entry
from the bibliography, even if it is not cited, add this YAML option:

```yaml
nocite: |
  @*
```

## Choose a citation style

A CSL file controls details such as citation order, punctuation, and whether
citations use author--date text or numbers. Download a style from the
[CSL style repository](https://github.com/citation-style-language/styles) and
save it with the manuscript. Then add its path to the same YAML header:

```yaml
bibliography: references.bib
csl: apa.csl
```

The YAML is identical in `.Rmd` and `.qmd` files. If `csl` is omitted, Pandoc
uses its default author--date style.

The CSL repository includes thousands of journal and publisher styles. Common
starting points include:

- [APA](https://github.com/citation-style-language/styles/blob/master/apa.csl)
  (`apa.csl`) for author--date citations;
- [Elsevier - Vancouver](https://github.com/citation-style-language/styles/blob/master/elsevier-vancouver.csl)
  (`elsevier-vancouver.csl`) for numbered biomedical citations;
- [Chicago author-date](https://github.com/citation-style-language/styles/blob/master/chicago-author-date.csl)
  (`chicago-author-date.csl`);
- [Nature](https://github.com/citation-style-language/styles/blob/master/nature.csl)
  (`nature.csl`) for numbered citations; and
- [IEEE](https://github.com/citation-style-language/styles/blob/master/ieee.csl)
  (`ieee.csl`) for bracketed numeric citations.

Use the repository's file search to find a journal-specific style. Download the
raw `.csl` file rather than saving the GitHub HTML page. Keeping the `.bib` and
`.csl` files under version control with the manuscript makes the rendered
references reproducible for collaborators.
